beats.say: Two teams want AI. Both need you first.
Merchandising wants a demand forecast.
beats.label: Team one
beats.head: A demand forecast

beats.say: And the product team wants a shopping assistant that answers from the catalog.
beats.label: Team two
beats.head: An assistant that knows the catalog

beats.say: Your job is to get the data ready. Three ideas.
beats.label: Station 4.2 · Data for AI and ML
beats.head: Get the data ready

check.prompt: You must forecast next month's demand from past sales. Which model type?
check.why: ARIMA_PLUS is the time series model in BigQuery ML.

beats.say: First: BigQuery ML. Machine learning, in SQL.
You write create model, and train it right where the data lives. No export.
beats.label: How

beats.say: To predict a number, use regression. For yes or no, classification. For groups with no labels, k-means.
beats.label: Pick the model type

beats.say: And for a forecast over time, like demand, use ARIMA PLUS.
beats.label: Time series
beats.head: Forecast: ARIMA_PLUS

beats.say: Put your clean-up steps in the transform clause. Then they run in training, and again at prediction.
beats.label: Feature engineering
beats.head: The TRANSFORM clause
beats.text: Same preprocessing at training and prediction

beats.say: The trap: exporting data to train a simple model somewhere else.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: Exporting data to train a simple model elsewhere

beats.say: Second: a few basics the exam still asks.
Overfitting is like a student who memorized last year's answers. Great in practice, lost in the real exam.
beats.label: Overfitting
beats.head: Memorized, did not learn

beats.say: The fixes: regularization, dropout, a simpler model, or more data.
beats.label: Fix overfitting

beats.say: With rare cases, like fraud, accuracy lies. Use precision and recall.
beats.label: Imbalanced data
beats.head: Accuracy lies. Use precision and recall.

beats.say: When behaviour changes over time, retrain on old and new data together. Not only the new.
beats.label: Drift
beats.head: Retrain on old + new data

check.prompt: How must you embed the questions and the documents?
options: Only the documents need a model
check.why: Vectors from different models cannot be compared.

beats.say: Third: the shopping assistant. This is called RAG.
The model does not know your catalog. So you look things up first, then let it answer.
beats.label: The idea
beats.head: Look it up, then answer

beats.say: Five steps. Chunk the documents. Embed them. Index the vectors. Retrieve. Then generate.
beats.label: The pipeline

beats.say: An embedding turns text into numbers, so that similar meanings sit close together.
beats.label: Embedding
beats.head: Similar meaning, close together

beats.say: In BigQuery, you can embed, index, and run vector search, all in SQL.
beats.label: Where
beats.head: Embed and search in BigQuery

beats.say: The trap: embedding questions with a different model than the documents.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: Use the same embedding model for questions and documents.

beats.say: Recap.
Train in SQL with create model. Fight overfitting. And for RAG, use one embedding model.
beats.label: Station 4.2
